questions.prompt: Use the squeeze theorem to evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}x^2\sin(1/x)\).
questions.answer:
For all allowed \(x\),
\[
-1\le \sin(1/x)\le1.
\]
Multiplying by \(x^2\ge0\) gives
\[
-x^2\le x^2\sin(1/x)\le x^2.
\]
Both bounds tend to \(0\), so the squeeze theorem gives
\[
\lim_{x\to0}x^2\sin(1/x)=0.
\]

The lower bound tends to
\[
\lim_{x\to0}(4-2x^2)=4,
\]
and the upper bound tends to
\[
\lim_{x\to0}(4+x^2)=4.
\]
Since both bounds tend to \(4\), the squeeze theorem gives
\[
\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=4.
\]

Since \(|\cos(7/x)|\le1\),
\[
\big||x|\cos(7/x)\big|\le |x|.
\]
As \(x\to0\), \(|x|\to0\). Therefore the absolute-value squeeze gives
\[
\lim_{x\to0}|x|\cos(7/x)=0.
\]
